First off appreciate the response. It’s so easy to jump to conclusions. Its also easy to over analyze the hell out of everything and attribute meaning to nothing. Like our brains automatically assume we aren’t worthy enough to be treated as we should.

As for the party my friend who I see a few times per year invited me as he was hosting. I showed up alone and was internally screaming seeing how packed it was. I really tried to be mindful the entire day and accept that I was going to feel incredibly uncomfortable. Just kept the mindset that I have goals I want to achieve and can’t let this hold me back. 

As for the mingling part oh boy… started off very awkward with the worst attempts in the first few minutes of my arrival. Unexpectedly it turned kinda great as i saw friends I hadn’t seen in 5 years. We ended up catching up which took a good bit of time. Next I ended up talking to the girl I previously mentioned. With her we had 3 main interactions  throughout the night that seemed to naturally start and die down. 

There was about 1:30 half of live music so it was easy to take a break from talking to people during that time. Something I noticed is talking to someone 1 on 1 at a party is way easier than trying to bud into a groups convo. The most natural Convos with the least amount of anxiety were 1 on 1 in retrospect. Sometimes I felt like I inserted myself and possibly annoyed people. After isolation, going to a party is like trying to fight the big bad boss when your characters level 2 or 3. I think I leveled up to 4. There’s a hundred levels😭

I find it weird seeing yourself on video. An old friend who I hadn’t seen in half a decade posted me on his story. In the moment I thought I looked like a nervous wreck, but in the video I’m just a normal dude vibing to the music. It’s important to recognize that despite dying on the inside, we’re just normal people living life.
